headline: Congress cancels an IRS rule that would have required decentralized crypto platforms to report users' digital asset sales to the IRS.
what_it_does: This law overturns an IRS rule issued on December 30, 2024. That rule would have treated certain providers of decentralized finance (DeFi) services as brokers. As brokers, they would have had to report information about digital asset sales, such as cryptocurrency trades, to the IRS. Under the Congressional Review Act, the rule now has no force or effect.

who_it_affects.group: Operators of decentralized finance (DeFi) crypto platforms
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to report the gross proceeds of users' digital asset sales to the IRS under this rule.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy and sell cryptocurrency through decentralized platforms
who_it_affects.how: Their sales on these platforms will not be reported to the IRS by the platform under this rule.
The agency loses this reporting requirement and cannot issue a substantially similar rule without new authority from Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: April 10, 2025, when the resolution was signed into law.
